hook: They say the dowry is **given willingly.** Is that still illegal?

slides.title: Giving is a **crime too.**
slides.body: Anyone who gives, takes, or helps give or take dowry is punishable: at least **five years** in jail, and a fine of at least ₹15,000 or the dowry's value, whichever is more.

slides.title: What **counts** as dowry?
slides.body: Any property or valuable security given or agreed to be given, directly or indirectly, at or before or any time after the marriage, in connection with the marriage. Mahr is excluded.

slides.title: Just **asking** is an offence.
slides.body: Demanding dowry, directly or indirectly, from the bride's or groom's parents, relatives or guardian: six months to two years in jail, and a fine of up to ₹10,000.

slides.title: Wedding gifts: **the narrow exception.**
list: Given at the wedding, without any demand
Entered in a list kept under the Rules
List in writing, signed by bride and groom
Bride's side gifts: customary, not excessive for the giver
slides.ref: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 · Sec 3(2); Dowry Prohibition (Lists of Presents) Rules 1985 · Rule 2

slides.title: Dowry **belongs to her.**
slides.body: If anyone other than the woman receives dowry, they must transfer it to her, generally **within three months.** Failing to do so is itself an offence.

slides.title: Treated **seriously.**
list: Accused must prove they didn't take or demand it
Cruelty for dowry: up to 3 years (BNS 85, 86)
slides.ref: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 · Sec 8(2), 8A; BNS 2023 · Sec 80, 85, 86

slides.title: Where to **complain.**
slides.body: Go to the police, or file a complaint with a Magistrate. The victim, a parent or relative, or a recognised welfare organisation can complain. States can appoint **Dowry Prohibition Officers.**
slides.note: Some States have amended this Act

sources: Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (as amended in 1984 and 1986) – Sections 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 8A, 8B
Dowry Prohibition (Maintenance of Lists of Presents to the Bride and Bridegroom) Rules, 1985 – Rule 2
Official copies: Women & Child Development Dept, Gujarat (wcd.gujarat.gov.in); NCRB, MHA (ncrb.mha.gov.in)
caption:
"We gave it willingly" is not a defence. Here's what the law says about dowry. 👇

1️⃣ Giving, taking or helping with dowry is a crime: at least 5 years in jail and a fine
2️⃣ Dowry means property or valuables given in connection with the marriage, before, at or after it
3️⃣ Even demanding dowry is punishable with up to 2 years in jail
4️⃣ Gifts given at the wedding without any demand are exempt only if listed; gifts from the bride's side must also be customary and not excessive
5️⃣ Any dowry received by others must be transferred to the woman
6️⃣ Complain to the police or a Magistrate; dowry cruelty and dowry death are offences under the BNS

Source: Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (Sec 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 8A, 8B); Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Sec 80, 85, 86)
